title: Domestication of the potato in the Andes
summary: Cultivated potatoes were probably first selected from wild Solanum relatives in the southern Andes of Peru, north of Lake Titicaca, between about 6,000 and 10,000 years ago. A second source places the origin in the Lake Titicaca region and notes that tubers were in use around 7,000 years ago.

uncertainty.note: Source says "between 6,000 and 10,000 years ago" (probable). Years ago are counted from the present and rounded to astronomical years -8000 to -4000; no calibration is stated. A second source gives tuber use around 7,000 years ago.

as_recorded.value: Las primeras papas cultivadas probablemente fueron seleccionadas entre 6.000 y 10.000 años atrás
Archaeological evidence shows that potato tubers were already used around 7000 years ago

where.modern_name: Lake Titicaca region, Peru and Bolivia (pin is the lake; source places selection north of the lake in southern Peru)
where.historical_name: Southern Andes, region around Lake Titicaca; no polities at this date

importance.justification: Origin of a crop now grown worldwide, from the Andean highlands.

sources.title: Origen y evolución de la papa cultivada. Una revisión (Origins and evolution of cultivated potato. A review)
sources.author: Luis Ernesto Rodríguez

sources.title: Origin and taxonomy of potato
sources.publisher: Centre for Genetic Resources, the Netherlands (CGN), Potato Genetic Resources Portal

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date: the main source says 6,000-10,000 years ago and "probably"; the second gives only 7,000 years for tuber use. The pin is Lake Titicaca (Wikidata), not an excavation site; the review places the first selection north of the lake in southern Peru while the second source says the region around the lake.
